title: Integration discovery - Cygnus AI
topics: Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private tradeoffs
summary: Intro discovery with Cygnus AI to understand integration surface for Redwood. Focus on LangChain/LlamaIndex adapters, proxying through an internal API gateway, per-route rate limits, and observability hooks. Customer is evaluating Hosted for speed, Dedicated for predictable throughput, and Private for data residency and SOC2 requirements. Next steps: share SDK examples, security pack, and propose pilot for a Dedicated mini-pool + integration checklist.
next_steps: Maya to share Redwood SDK quickstart + LangChain/LlamaIndex examples by 2026-10-16
Jon to schedule a technical deep-dive (SE-led) for model sharding and kv cache on 2026-10-20
Maya to send Dedicated pricing and pilot contract template by 2026-10-18
Customer to provide sample traffic profile and sensitive data list by 2026-10-19

Jon - Prepare SE-deep-dive slide deck covering batching, kv cache, and quantization options - 2026-10-19

transcript:
Header: 2026-10-14 15:00 PST | Duration: ~46m
Attendees: Maya (Redwood AE), Jon (Redwood SE), Sofia (Redwood Solutions); Lena (CTO, Cygnus), Ravi (Lead ML Eng), Aaron (Platform), Mei (Security)

00:00:03 Maya: Hey everyone, thanks for taking the time, quick round of intros then we'll dig into the integration surface.
00:00:12 Lena: Hi, I'm Lena, CTO at Cygnus, we build domain-specific agents for telecom automation. Ravi will lead on infra questions.
00:00:18 Ravi: Yep, hi all.
00:00:20 Maya: Awesome. Jon, want to give a quick run on what we'll cover?
00:00:25 Jon: Sure - we'll walk SDKs, LangChain/LlamaIndex support, how folks typically proxy through gateways, rate limiting and quotas, and the observability hooks you can attach. We'll also talk Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private tradeoffs.
00:00:40 Aaron: One note up front, we have strict network egress policies and most traffic must go via our internal API gateway, so any hosted solution needs to play nice with that.
00:00:50 Jon: Totally understood, we've seen that before; we can either route via customer gateway with a proxy or run Redwood Private in their VPC for air-gapped like setups.
00:01:05 Ravi: Can you clarify the SDK story? We use LangChain and LlamaIndex heavily.
00:01:12 Maya: Redwood SDKs have first-class LangChain adapters and an official LlamaIndex connector. Example repos live on GitHub, we have quickstarts for both sync and async flows. We'll share links after.
00:01:24 Ravi: Are those wrappers or do they stream tokens the same as your REST API?
00:01:30 Jon: They wrap the streaming endpoints and expose the same token-streaming semantics. You can attach custom callbacks in LangChain to push tokens into your local websocket. Small caveat: some older community LangChain versions had differing callback signatures, so check the adapter branch.
00:01:50 Lena: For deployment, if we run in VPC (Private) we need KMS integration for keys and audit logs forwarded to our SIEM. Is that supported?
00:02:01 Sofia: Yes - Private mode supports customer-managed KMS/HSM and audit log forwarding. We also support an on-prem package if needed. We'll share the compliance packet.
00:02:12 Mei: What's the difference between Dedicated and Private in terms of network egress?
00:02:18 Jon: Dedicated is reserved capacity in Redwood's cloud but still outbound from Redwood infra; Private is a customer-controlled VPC/private control plane. If you want no egress to public internet, Private or on-prem is the path. Dedicated can be configured with VPC peering for tighter networking, but not fully air-gapped.
00:02:40 Aaron: Good to know. About gateway/proxy: our router terminates TLS and imposes per-route rate limits. Can we front Redwood with that?
00:02:48 Maya: Yes, you can sit your gateway in front of the Redwood hosted endpoints. You'd use API keys scoped to routes and our rate-limit headers (x-rl-remaining etc) are surfaced so you can integrate. We can also support JWT-based auth if you prefer.
00:03:10 Ravi: How coarse are your rate limits? We need per-customer and per-route limits — plus burst handling.
00:03:18 Jon: We support per-api-key quotas and per-route SLOs. For Hosted, quotas are per-account and per-key; for Dedicated you can configure per-tenant isolation policies inside the pool. We have burst windows; for very high spikes we recommend Dedicated with auto-burst nodes to keep latency SLOs.
00:03:36 Lena: We're sensitive to latency for live agent responses (sub-200ms token latency target). Can Redwood hit that?
00:03:44 Jon: Sub-200ms is tough for long-context generation on some models; for condensed responses and optimized kernels, some of our configs on Dedicated can achieve ~120-180ms p99 for small models. Hosted has more variability. Caching, prefix KV caching, and batching policies help.
00:04:05 Ravi: You mentioned KV cache — how does that integrate with LangChain memory?
00:04:12 Jon: KV cache is internal token/key-value cache at model inference time — it's not the same as LangChain memory. LangChain memory persists higher-level embeddings/metadata; our KV cache reduces repeated compute on the same prefix, which helps with costs and latency. You can use both.
00:04:30 Aaron: If we use our gateway and do prefix caching on our side, will Redwood's cache conflict?
00:04:36 Jon: Not really — your gateway caching is at HTTP request level; our KV cache is model-internal. They complement each other. We can tune cache TTLs and invalidation.
00:04:50 Ravi: Observability — do you expose tracing headers for correlating requests across our systems?
00:04:55 Sofia: Yes, we surface trace IDs and support distributed tracing headers. You can attach X-Trace-Id and it will show up in Redwood Console traces. We also export metrics via Prometheus endpoints for Dedicated and Private.
00:05:10 Mei: Do logs include PII? We have strict retention and redaction rules.
00:05:16 Maya: For Hosted, we redact user-provided inputs by default and have retention controls. For Private, logs live in your control plane and you determine retention and redaction. We'll send the security docs that list exact fields stored.
00:05:30 Lena: On the SDK side, what's the recommended pattern for large-context retrieval with LlamaIndex? We have 50k token contexts in some flows.
00:05:40 Jon: For very large context you should chunk and use embeddings + a retrieval step (LlamaIndex or vectordb) to populate the prompt window. We also provide streaming windowing helpers in the SDK to handle progressive retrieval. For extremely long context you might need model sharding or recency windows; that's where Dedicated + higher memory instances help.
00:06:05 Ravi: Model variants — if we need quantized models for cost, do you maintain those or do we bring our own?
00:06:12 Sofia: We provide curated quantized profiles for many open models and can recommend quantization levels per workload. Dedicated allows you to pin model variants; Private supports your BYO model in many cases but there are infra constraints.
00:06:26 Aaron: Does Redwood support BYO models with private weights? We have custom finetunes.
00:06:31 Jon: Private and certain Dedicated deployments support customer model uploads with encrypted storage and HSM-backed keys. For Hosted we can host finetunes under enterprise agreements, but Private is the most straightforward for BYO.
00:06:45 Lena: Regarding quotas, how do you handle overages and soft-failures? We need graceful degradation.
00:06:52 Maya: We have policy-based fallbacks — you can set automatic fallback to smaller models or cached responses when limits are hit. Also rate limit headers and webhook alerts. For mission-critical flows we usually recommend Dedicated with buffer capacity.
00:07:10 Ravi: Are there per-route analytics available in Console? We need token-level cost breakdown by route and model.
00:07:16 Sofia: Yes, Redwood Console shows per-route token counts, latency distributions, and cost by model. You can export to BigQuery or S3.
00:07:26 Aaron: How intrusive is the SDK to swap in? We have a Java microservices stack and some Python workers.
00:07:32 Jon: SDKs are available in Python, Node, and Java (beta). For microservices you can call our HTTP endpoints directly; the SDK mainly simplifies streaming and retries. For LangChain/LlamaIndex, the Python SDK is the smoothest.
00:07:45 Ravi: For experiments we'll want a small POC — say 2-3 models, some traffic replay, and end-to-end tracing. Can Redwood help run benchmarks?
00:07:53 Maya: Absolutely. We usually do a benchmark run: you provide traffic profile, sample prompts, and we'll run them on Hosted and Dedicated and share latency/cost comparisons and token breakdowns.
00:08:03 Lena: Any gotchas with proxies and websockets? We use websocket multiplexing for agent comms.
00:08:09 Jon: Hosted streaming supports SSE and websocket; if your gateway blocks websockets, SSE over HTTP works. We sometimes see proxies drop long-lived websockets; we recommend health-checking and reconnect logic.
00:08:26 Ravi: What about rate limiting at token granularity or per-request?
00:08:31 Sofia: We rate limit on requests and tokens for billing. Per-token limits are mostly internal for fairness; quotas are expressed as tokens/day or requests/minute per key. For Dedicated you can get more flexible SLA'd throughput.
00:08:44 Aaron: For observability hooks, can we run our own exporters inside Dedicated nodes?
00:08:49 Jon: You can sidecar exporters for metrics in Dedicated and Private; we support Prometheus scraping and pushing to your metrics pipeline. For Hosted we expose ingestion endpoints and integrations with Datadog, but you can't run sidecars in hosted.
00:09:05 Lena: Security review: Mei will need SOC2 evidence, network diagrams, data flow and encryption details. Can you send those docs?
00:09:13 Maya: Yes, we'll send the security pack and SOC2 report. For Private deployments we'll provide architecture diagrams and options for on-prem.
00:09:22 Ravi: On pricing, we need to understand committed vs usage-based; we'd likely start with a small Dedicated pilot.
00:09:28 Maya: We can do a Reserved mini-pool pilot (1-2 GPUs sized for your traffic) with a short-term committed trial and portal to monitor cost. We'll send pricing tiers.
00:09:40 Aaron: One implementation detail — our auth flow requires mTLS to internal services. Does Redwood support mTLS to endpoints?
00:09:47 Jon: For Private and Dedicated with VPC peering, yes we support mTLS. For Hosted we support TLS + JWT and IP allowlists, but mTLS is typically only available in Private.
00:09:59 Mei: Data residency — we need EU-only processing for a subset of customers.
00:10:05 Sofia: We have region pinning and can run workloads in EU-only regions; Private is easiest for full residency guarantees.
00:10:13 Lena: Great. Can you walk quickly through a sample flow integrating LangChain?
00:10:18 Jon: Quick flow: 1) Use LlamaIndex to build an index from your docs -> embeddings stored in your vector DB; 2) LLM call goes through Redwood SDK (LangChain wrapper) with the retrieved chunks; 3) LangChain memory updated as needed; 4) If you have a gateway, it proxies the call and adds trace headers. We can share a gist.
00:10:45 Ravi: For rate-limiting tests, we need a test account with high qps.
00:10:50 Maya: We'll enable a test key for your POC with increased quotas for benchmark runs.
00:10:55 Lena: Any constraints on max context length in your endpoints?
00:10:59 Jon: Depends on model; we support up to 128k context for some models in Dedicated/Private via windowed streaming and chunking. Hosted top-end models vary.
00:11:13 Aaron: About logs — are raw prompts stored in Hosted? We need redaction.
00:11:19 Maya: Hosted redact-by-default, but you can opt-in to retain full inputs for debugging; retention windows configurable under enterprise agreements.
00:11:27 Mei: What SSO options for Console access? SAML, OIDC?
00:11:31 Sofia: SAML, OIDC, SCIM provisioning and RBAC support are available for Dedicated and Hosted enterprise accounts. Private integrates with your IdP.
00:11:44 Ravi: Regarding integration complexity, what does a typical POC timeline look like?
00:11:48 Maya: Usually 2-4 weeks: week 1 onboarding + sample traffic, week 2 benchmark and integration, week 3 iterate on tuning and security review, week 4 decision.
00:11:59 Lena: That aligns. Any customers in telco space?
00:12:03 Maya: Yes, Gamma Telecom and Vertex Telecom are telco customers; we can intro under NDA.
00:12:11 Ravi: Can you show the Console live? Maybe in the SE-deep-dive.
00:12:15 Jon: We'll demo the Console in the technical deep-dive. It shows traces, token-cost per route, and rollout controls.
00:12:23 Maya: Quick check — are there any blockers from your side to start a pilot?
00:12:27 Aaron: We need the security pack and a whitepaper on proxy patterns. Also a test key with higher qps.
00:12:33 Mei: And SOC2 evidence.
00:12:36 Maya: We'll send those.
00:12:38 Lena: Good.
00:12:40 [silence / typing]
00:14:05 Jon: (demo note) One thing to highlight — our rate-limit headers include x-rd-rl-limit and x-rd-rl-remaining, and we have webhooks for quota-exhausted events.
00:16:22 Ravi: A question on SDK auth — if we use short-lived tokens should we rotate keys frequently?
00:16:30 Sofia: Short-lived JWTs are recommended; we support key rotation and session tokens. For long-running platform services, mTLS or dedicated API keys in VPC are used.
00:18:45 Aaron: If we want to forward trace IDs, any header naming conventions?
00:18:50 Jon: X-Trace-Id works, we also accept traceparent for W3C distributed tracing.
00:20:02 Lena: On the topic of deployment, if we go Dedicated, can we reserve capacity in a specific region and set auto-burst on?
00:20:09 Maya: Yes, you can reserve in region and set autoscaling and burst pools. Burst uses additional capacity that may have different pricing.
00:21:33 Ravi: For LlamaIndex connector, do you support async retrieval and streaming of partial results?
00:21:39 Jon: Yes, the connector supports async retrieval; streaming partial results is possible via chunked streaming and callback hooks. There's a sample in the repo.
00:23:50 Aaron: Any limits on model uploads size? We have a 50GB finetune artifact.
00:23:56 Sofia: For Private and Dedicated we can handle large artifacts; for Hosted there are quotas. We'll include upload guidelines.
00:26:10 Maya: Recap: we'll send SDK quickstarts, security pack, Dedicated pricing, and enable a test key. Jon will run the SE deep-dive and demo the Console on 2026-10-20.
00:26:28 Lena: Sounds good.
00:26:30 Ravi: One more thing — do you have examples of gateway header rewrites for client IP preservation?
00:26:36 Jon: Yes, we have a pattern for X-Forwarded-For and audit fields; we'll include that in the integration doc.
00:28:12 Maya: Anything else?
00:28:15 Aaron: No, thanks.
00:28:17 Mei: We'll review the security pack once received.
00:28:20 Maya: Great. Thanks everyone. We'll follow up with next steps and materials.
00:45:40 [call ends]
